:::{#exm-taylor-mv}
#### For a quadratic form the expansion is exact

Let $f(\vx) = \qform{\matr{S}}{\vx}$ with $\matr{S}$ symmetric and constant.
Its [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) is $\gradf{f}(\vx) = 2 \matr{S} \vx$
([quadratic form gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#cor-quadratic-form-symmetric))
and its [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) is $2 \matr{S}$ at every point
([quadratic form Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#thm-hessian-quadratic)),
so whatever $\midpt$ is, @thm-taylor-mv reads

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vecf{z} + \vecf{h})
&= \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} + \tp{(2 \matr{S} \vecf{z})} \vecf{h} + \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}} (2 \matr{S}) \vecf{h} \\
&= \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{h} + \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{h},
\end{aligned}
$$

using

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tp{(2 \matr{S} \vecf{z})} &= 2\,\tp{\vecf{z}}\,\tp{\matr{S}} \\
&= 2\,\tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying out directly gives the same:

$$
\ba
\tp{(\vecf{z} + \vecf{h})} \matr{S} (\vecf{z} + \vecf{h})
&= \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} + \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{h} + \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} + \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{h}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{h} + \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{h}.
&& \text{(} \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{z} = \tp{(\tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{S} \vecf{z})} \text{, which equals } \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{S} \vecf{h} \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
